burnExplanation: A team that's 95% safe with zero future value (dead next round) scores 8.6. That same team as a Final Four contender scores 0.95. Same safety, wildly different burn value.
oneRule: Every time you pick a team, ask: Will I wish I had this team later? Yes → find someone else. No → burn them.

rounds.name: FINAL FOUR
rounds.verdict: Houston (beats UConn in semifinal, then falls to Michigan in Championship)

candidates.analysis: Houston's defense smothers a UConn team still reeling from St. John's 72-52 Big East blowout. Sampson's physicality exploits the exact interior weakness Ejiofor exposed. If your format requires a F4 pick, Houston is the play — they beat UConn but fall to Michigan in the final.

If your format requires a semifinal pick, you COULD use Michigan here — but you'll need them for the Championship. Michigan's size advantage overwhelms Arizona's 7-man attack. Only burn Michigan in the F4 if your pool doesn't require a Championship pick.
AVOID. The 72-52 Big East tournament loss to St. John's was a red flag, not a blip. Houston's defense is a worse version of the same matchup problem. UConn's interior vulnerability is real.

AVOID. Arizona is elite but Michigan's #1 defense and size advantage (Mara 7-3) is the worst possible matchup. Arizona's 7-man attack gets one shot per possession against Michigan's rebounding dominance.

rounds.name: CHAMPIONSHIP
rounds.verdict: Deploy your champion. Michigan over Houston.

candidates.analysis: Deploy your champion. Michigan's interior dominance (Mara 7-3, Lendeborg 6-9) overwhelms Houston's elite defense. The two best defenses in America clash, but Michigan's size creates the margin. Lendeborg finishes with 21/12/4 for MOP. Dusty May cuts down the nets. Michigan 65-59.
